body:
Thanks file filing an issue. In order to investigate, we will need the following information:
1. What version of ESLint are you using?
2. What source code are you linting? Please give exact code if possible.
3. How do you have this rule configured?
To give it an update, it still exists in 0.19.0.
Yup, the issue is still open so it hasn't been dealt with yet.

I think this syntax is incorrect, with that being said It should flag as an syntax error rather than error out. After investigating more I found out the library `doctrine` doesnt thow an syntax error.
I have opened an issue with them asking the question here : https://github.com/Constellation/doctrine/issues/106
If they fix this on their side (ideally they should) then we dont need to make any change, if not then we need to handle this.
It's not a syntax error - that's valid JSDoc (the type is not required). This is a bug in our rule that should be fixed.

but its a syntax error if you do the same for `returns` tag.
That's why I thought this might be a bad syntax.
I'm not sure about `returns`, but I know `param` definitely doesn't require a type. We are probably throwing an error because we are assuming a type will be there.
Ah, yeah, that's definitely a parser bug.

issue.title: Crash in valid-jsdoc with invalid JSDoc

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
Seeing a crash in valid-jsdoc.js:

```
eslint\lib\rules\valid-jsdoc.js:126
                        } else if (tag.name.indexOf(".") === -1) {
                                           ^

TypeError: Cannot read property 'indexOf' of undefined
    at eslint\lib\rules\valid-jsdoc.js:126:44
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at EventEmitter.checkJSDoc (eslint\lib\rules\valid-jsdoc.js:107:24)
```

It appears that this invalid JSDoc triggers the crash:

```
/**
 * Descr
 * @param arg1 [optional] description
 */
```

Basically, the `[optional]` text confuses the parser and makes it so there is no `tag.name`.
